_note: RANKED METRO UNIVERSE for the rigging/machinery-moving lead engine. tier 1 = 48 live city hubs (in locations.json). tier 2 = next wave. tier 3 = expansion. status 'live' = city hub already built; 'queued' = to add in waves. 'industry' = the real industrial driver that makes each page genuinely local (uniqueness-engine input). Crane & heavy-haul city variants intentionally EXCLUDED per cluster analysis (unwinnable vs national incumbents). Review/approve before wiring to generators.

metros.industry: heavy manufacturing & the nation's rail hub
GE Aviation, machine tools & advanced manufacturing

_detailNote: PER-METRO SUBSTANCE, researched 2026-09-21. This is the matrix differentiation fix. A service x city page runs ~1,550 words and the only per-city input used to be the 4-word 'industry' string above (Omaha: 'rail & ag manufacturing'), which measured the four city matrices at 31-32% page-specific content against a 33% floor, with 86-88 of 113 pages under it. build-service-cities.js now reads these fields and each service frames them in its own words - see METRO_COPY there, and note that each service deliberately draws a DIFFERENT mix so the same facts do not produce the same sentences across four pages for one city. Every value is a verifiable public fact: named industrial districts and parks, the Class I railroads that actually serve the metro, real navigable freight water access, the dominant industrial building stock. An absent field means the research could not confirm it - 'port' is absent for inland metros by design, and 15 metros have no 'stock'. NEVER add an unverified fact here: it lands on four live pages per metro, and an unverifiable claim repeated across 88 metros is worse than a generic one. Metros with no entry keep their previous page output byte-for-byte.
